sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca tam apratimasattvaujobalavīryaparākramam hataṃ devavrataṃ śrutvā pāñcālyena śikhaṇḍinā
english: Janamejaya said: When he had heard that Devavrata—peerless in courage, vigor, strength, valor, and prowess—had been slain by Śikhaṇḍin the Pāñcāla,

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭras tadā rājā śokavyākulacetanaḥ kim aceṣṭata viprarṣe hate pitari vīryavān
english: what then did King Dhṛtarāṣṭra do, his mind distraught with grief, O sage among brahmins, when that valiant father of his had fallen?

sanskrit: tasya putro hi bhagavan bhīṣmadroṇamukhai rathaiḥ parājitya maheṣvāsān pāṇḍavān rājyam icchati
english: For his son, O reverend one, sought the kingdom by overcoming the great-bowed Pāṇḍavas with chariot-warriors led by Bhīṣma and Droṇa.

sanskrit: tasmin hate tu bhagavan ketau sarvadhanuṣmatām yad aceṣṭata kauravyas tan me brūhi dvijottama
english: Now that he was slain, O reverend one—he who was the banner of all bowmen—tell me what the Kaurava did, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca nihataṃ pitaraṃ śrutvā dhṛtarāṣṭro janādhipaḥ lebhe na śāntiṃ kauravyaś cintāśokaparāyaṇaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing that his father was slain, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of men, found no peace—that Kaurava, given over wholly to anxiety and grief.

sanskrit: tasya cintayato duḥkham aniśaṃ pārthivasya tat ājagāma viśuddhātmā punar gāvalgaṇis tadā
english: As the king brooded ceaselessly upon that sorrow, the pure-souled son of Gavalgaṇa came once more before him.

sanskrit: śibirāt saṃjayaṃ prāptaṃ niśi nāgāhvayaṃ puram āmbikeyo mahārāja dhṛtarāṣṭro 'nvapṛcchata
english: When Saṃjaya had come by night from the camp to the city named for the elephant, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Ambikā, questioned him, O great king.

sanskrit: śrutvā bhīṣmasya nidhanam aprahṛṣṭamanā bhṛśam putrāṇāṃ jayam ākāṅkṣan vilalāpāturo yathā
english: Hearing of Bhīṣma's death, his heart utterly without joy, yet longing for the victory of his sons, he lamented as one stricken.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca saṃsādhya tu mahātmānaṃ bhīṣmaṃ bhīmaparākramam kim akārṣuḥ paraṃ tāta kuravaḥ kālacoditāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When they had overcome the great-souled Bhīṣma of terrible prowess, what then did the Kurus do, my son, urged on by fate?

sanskrit: tasmin vinihate śūre durādharṣe mahaujasi kiṃ nu svit kuravo 'kārṣur nimagnāḥ śokasāgare
english: When that hero—unassailable, of mighty energy—was struck down, what did the Kurus do, sunk in an ocean of grief?

sanskrit: tad udīrṇaṃ mahat sainyaṃ trailokyasyāpi saṃjaya bhayam utpādayet tīvraṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām
english: That great army of the high-souled Pāṇḍavas, once roused, could strike fierce terror even into the three worlds, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: devavrate tu nihate kurūṇām ṛṣabhe tadā yad akārṣur nṛpatayas tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: When Devavrata, that bull of the Kurus, was slain, tell me what the kings then did, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śṛṇu rājann ekamanā vacanaṃ bruvato mama yat te putrās tadākārṣur hate devavrate mṛdhe
english: Saṃjaya said: Hear, O king, with single mind the words I speak—what your sons did when Devavrata had fallen in the fray.

sanskrit: nihate tu tadā bhīṣme rājan satyaparākrame tāvakāḥ pāṇḍaveyāś ca prādhyāyanta pṛthak pṛthak
english: When Bhīṣma of truthful prowess was slain, O king, both your men and the Pāṇḍavas fell to brooding, each side apart.

sanskrit: vismitāś ca prahṛṣṭāś ca kṣatradharmaṃ niśāmya te svadharmaṃ nindamānāś ca praṇipatya mahātmane
english: Amazed and yet exultant, beholding the law of the warrior, and reproaching their own calling, they bowed down before that great soul.

sanskrit: śayanaṃ kalpayām āsur bhīṣmāyāmitatejase sopadhānaṃ naravyāghra śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: They made ready a bed for Bhīṣma of measureless splendor, O tiger among men, with a pillow too, fashioned of arrows with bent-down joints.

sanskrit: vidhāya rakṣāṃ bhīṣmāya samābhāṣya parasparam anumānya ca gāṅgeyaṃ kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam
english: Having set a guard about Bhīṣma, and spoken each with the other, and taken leave of the son of Gaṅgā, and walked round him in reverence,

sanskrit: krodhasaṃraktanayanāḥ samavekṣya parasparam punar yuddhāya nirjagmuḥ kṣatriyāḥ kālacoditāḥ
english: their eyes red with wrath, the warriors, gazing upon one another, marched forth again to battle, driven on by fate.

sanskrit: tatas tūryaninādaiś ca bherīṇāṃ ca mahāsvanaiḥ tāvakānām anīkāni pareṣāṃ cāpi niryayuḥ
english: Then to the blare of trumpets and the great booming of war-drums, the divisions of your host and of the foe alike went forth.

sanskrit: vyāvṛtte 'hani rājendra patite jāhnavīsute amarṣavaśam āpannāḥ kālopahatacetasaḥ
english: As the day turned, O lord of kings, with the son of Jāhnavī fallen, they yielded to fury, their minds undone by fate.

sanskrit: anādṛtya vacaḥ pathyaṃ gāṅgeyasya mahātmanaḥ niryayur bharataśreṣṭhāḥ śastrāṇy ādāya sarvaśaḥ
english: Heedless of the wholesome counsel of the great-souled son of Gaṅgā, the foremost of the Bhāratas marched out, taking up their weapons on every side.

sanskrit: mohāt tava saputrasya vadhāc chāṃtanavasya ca kauravyā mṛtyusād bhūtāḥ sahitāḥ sarvarājabhiḥ
english: Through your folly and that of your sons, and through the slaying of the son of Śaṃtanu, the Kauravas, together with all their kings, were made over to death.

sanskrit: ajāvaya ivāgopā vane śvāpadasaṃkule bhṛśam udvignamanaso hīnā devavratena te
english: Like sheep and goats without a herdsman in a forest thronged with beasts of prey, their hearts deeply troubled, were they, bereft of Devavrata.

sanskrit: patite bharataśreṣṭhe babhūva kuruvāhinī dyaur ivāpetanakṣatrā hīnaṃ kham iva vāyunā
english: When the foremost of the Bhāratas had fallen, the Kuru host became like a sky with its stars departed, like the firmament without wind.

sanskrit: vipannasasyeva mahī vāk caivāsaṃskṛtā yathā āsurīva yathā senā nigṛhīte purā balau
english: like the earth with its harvest withered, like speech left unrefined, like the army of the Asuras of old when Bali was overthrown.

sanskrit: vidhaveva varārohā śuṣkatoyeva nimnagā vṛkair iva vane ruddhā pṛṣatī hatayūthapā
english: like a fair-hipped woman widowed, like a river with its waters dried, like a spotted doe whose herd-leader is slain, hemmed in by wolves in the wood,

sanskrit: svādharṣā hatasiṃheva mahatī girikandarā bhāratī bharataśreṣṭha patite jāhnavīsute
english: like a great mountain-cavern, once unassailable, with its lion slain—such, O best of the Bhāratas, was the host of Bhārata when the son of Jāhnavī had fallen.

sanskrit: viṣvagvātahatā rugṇā naur ivāsīn mahārṇave balibhiḥ pāṇḍavair vīrair labdhalakṣair bhṛśārditā
english: It was like a ship battered and broken by winds from every quarter on the great sea, sorely afflicted by the mighty Pāṇḍava heroes who had found their mark.

sanskrit: sā tadāsīd bhṛśaṃ senā vyākulāśvarathadvipā viṣaṇṇabhūyiṣṭhanarā kṛpaṇā draṣṭum ābabhau
english: That army then was sorely shaken, its horses, chariots, and elephants in disarray, most of its men downcast; pitiful it appeared to behold.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ trastā nṛpatayaḥ sainikāś ca pṛthagvidhāḥ pātāla iva majjanto hīnā devavratena te karṇaṃ hi kuravo 'smārṣuḥ sa hi devavratopamaḥ
english: Within it the kings and soldiers of every kind were filled with dread, sinking as if into the nether world, bereft of Devavrata; and so the Kurus called Karṇa to mind, for he was the equal of Devavrata.

sanskrit: sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ rocamānam ivātithim bandhum āpadgatasyeva tam evopāgaman manaḥ
english: To him, the foremost of all who bear arms, shining like a welcome guest, like a kinsman to one fallen into peril—to him their thoughts turned.

sanskrit: cukruśuḥ karṇa karṇeti tatra bhārata pārthivāḥ rādheyaṃ hitam asmākaṃ sūtaputraṃ tanutyajam
english: "Karṇa! Karṇa!" the kings cried out there, O Bhārata—the son of Rādhā, our well-wisher, the charioteer's son who would lay down his very body for us.

sanskrit: sa hi nāyudhyata tadā daśāhāni mahāyaśāḥ sāmātyabandhuḥ karṇo vai tam āhvayata māciram
english: For he of great renown, Karṇa, had not fought for those ten days, he and his counselors and kinsmen; "Summon him without delay!"

sanskrit: bhīṣmeṇa hi mahābāhuḥ sarvakṣatrasya paśyataḥ ratheṣu gaṇyamāneṣu balavikramaśāliṣu saṃkhyāto 'rdharathaḥ karṇo dviguṇaḥ san nararṣabhaḥ
english: For Bhīṣma, before the eyes of all the warriors, when the chariot-warriors endowed with strength and valor were being reckoned, had counted the mighty-armed Karṇa—that bull among men, though twofold in might—as but half a chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: rathātirathasaṃkhyāyāṃ yo 'graṇīḥ śūrasaṃmataḥ pitṛvittāmbudeveśān api yo yoddhum utsahet
english: —he who in the reckoning of chariot-warriors and great chariot-warriors stood foremost, esteemed of heroes, who would dare to do battle even with the lords of the fathers, of wealth, of waters, and of the gods.

sanskrit: sa tu tenaiva kopena rājan gāṅgeyam uktavān tvayi jīvati kauravya nāhaṃ yotsye kathaṃ cana
english: And it was through that very anger, O king, that Karṇa had said to the son of Gaṅgā: "While you live, O Kaurava, I will not fight at all.

sanskrit: tvayā tu pāṇḍaveyeṣu nihateṣu mahāmṛdhe duryodhanam anujñāpya vanaṃ yāsyāmi kaurava
english: But when by you the Pāṇḍavas have been slain in the great battle, I shall take leave of Duryodhana and go to the forest, O Kaurava.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavair vā hate bhīṣme tvayi svargam upeyuṣi hantāsmy ekarathenaiva kṛtsnān yān manyase rathān
english: Or if Bhīṣma is slain by the Pāṇḍavas, and you have gone to heaven, then I alone, with a single chariot, will slay all those whom you account chariot-warriors."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahārāja daśāhāni mahāyaśāḥ nāyudhyata tataḥ karṇaḥ putrasya tava saṃmate
english: Having spoken thus, O great king, the illustrious Karṇa fought not for ten days, by the consent of your son.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaḥ samaravikrāntaḥ pāṇḍaveyasya pārthiva jaghāna samare yodhān asaṃkhyeyaparākramaḥ
english: Bhīṣma, valiant in battle, O king, of prowess beyond all counting, slew countless warriors of the Pāṇḍava host in the field.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu nihate śūre satyasaṃdhe mahaujasi tvatsutāḥ karṇam asmārṣus tartukāmā iva plavam
english: But when that hero, true to his word and of mighty energy, was slain, your sons called Karṇa to mind, as men longing to cross the water think of a raft.

sanskrit: tāvakās tava putrāś ca sahitāḥ sarvarājabhiḥ hā karṇa iti cākrandan kālo 'yam iti cābruvan
english: Your men and your sons, together with all the kings, cried out "Alas, Karṇa!" and said, "This is the hour."

sanskrit: jāmadagnyābhyanujñātam astre durvārapauruṣam agaman no manaḥ karṇaṃ bandhum ātyayikeṣv iva
english: To Karṇa—sanctioned in arms by the son of Jamadagni, of manhood not to be withstood—our thoughts went out, as to a kinsman in times of dire need.

sanskrit: sa hi śakto raṇe rājaṃs trātum asmān mahābhayāt tridaśān iva govindaḥ satataṃ sumahābhayāt
english: For he was able in battle, O king, to save us from great peril, as Govinda ever saved the thirty gods from exceeding great peril.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā karṇaṃ yudhi varaṃ kīrtayantaṃ punaḥ punaḥ āśīviṣavad ucchvasya dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bravīd idam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As Saṃjaya thus praised Karṇa again and again as the best in battle, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, hissing like a venomous serpent, spoke these words:

sanskrit: yat tad vaikartanaṃ karṇam agamad vo manas tadā apy apaśyata rādheyaṃ sūtaputraṃ tanutyajam
english: "When your thoughts then went out to Karṇa, son of the sun, did you indeed see the son of Rādhā, the charioteer's son who would yield up his body?

sanskrit: api tan na mṛṣākārṣīd yudhi satyaparākramaḥ saṃbhrāntānāṃ tadārtānāṃ trastānāṃ trāṇam icchatām
english: Did he, of truthful prowess, not prove false to it in battle—to those bewildered, stricken, and afraid, who looked to him for deliverance?

sanskrit: api tat pūrayāṃ cakre dhanurdharavaro yudhi yat tad vinihate bhīṣme kauravāṇām apāvṛtam
english: Did that best of bowmen fill in battle the breach that had been laid open among the Kauravas when Bhīṣma was slain?

sanskrit: tat khaṇḍaṃ pūrayām āsa pareṣām ādadhad bhayam kṛtavān mama putrāṇāṃ jayāśāṃ saphalām api
english: Did he fill that gap, striking dread into the foe, and make fruitful at last the hope of victory of my sons?"

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hataṃ bhīṣmam ādhirathir viditvā; bhinnāṃ nāvam ivātyagādhe kurūṇām sodaryavad vyasanāt sūtaputraḥ; saṃtārayiṣyaṃs tava putrasya senām
english: Saṃjaya said: When the son of Adhiratha learned that Bhīṣma was slain—the host of the Kurus like a shattered ship upon a bottomless deep—that charioteer's son, like a brother in their calamity, set out to bear your son's army across to safety.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu karṇaḥ puruṣendram acyutaṃ; nipātitaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ mahāratham athopāyāt tūrṇam amitrakarśano; dhanurdharāṇāṃ pravaras tadā vṛṣaḥ
english: And Karṇa, hearing that the lord of men, the unfailing son of Śaṃtanu, that great chariot-warrior, had been struck down, came swiftly forth, that scourge of foes, the bull and foremost among bowmen.

sanskrit: hate tu bhīṣme rathasattame parair; nimajjatīṃ nāvam ivārṇave kurūn piteva putrāṃs tvarito 'bhyayāt tataḥ; saṃtārayiṣyaṃs tava putrasya senām
english: When Bhīṣma, best of chariot-warriors, was slain by the foe, he hastened to the Kurus, who were sinking like a ship in the sea—as a father to his sons—to bear your son's army across to safety.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca yasmin dhṛtir buddhiparākramaujo; damaḥ satyaṃ vīraguṇāś ca sarve astrāṇi divyāny atha saṃnatir hrīḥ; priyā ca vāg anapāyīni bhīṣme
english: Karṇa said: In whom dwelt steadfastness, wisdom, valor, and energy, self-mastery, truth, and all a hero's virtues, divine weapons, humility, modesty, and gracious speech—all unfailing in Bhīṣma;

sanskrit: brahmadviṣaghne satataṃ kṛtajñe; sanātanaṃ candramasīva lakṣma sa cet praśāntaḥ paravīrahantā; manye hatān eva hi sarvayodhān
english: in him, the ever-slayer of those who hate the brahmins, the ever-grateful, in whom virtue was eternal as the mark upon the moon—if he, the slayer of enemy heroes, is now stilled, then I deem all our warriors already slain.

sanskrit: neha dhruvaṃ kiṃ cana jātu vidyate; asmiṃl loke karmaṇo 'nityayogāt sūryodaye ko hi vimuktasaṃśayo; bhāvaṃ kurvītādya mahāvrate hate
english: Nothing here is ever found to be fixed, by reason of the impermanence that cleaves to all deeds in this world. Who, when the great-vowed one is slain, could at sunrise today, free of doubt, count on any thing's enduring?

sanskrit: vasuprabhāve vasuvīryasaṃbhave; gate vasūn eva vasuṃdharādhipe vasūni putrāṃś ca vasuṃdharāṃ tathā; kurūṃś ca śocadhvam imāṃ ca vāhinīm
english: Now that the lord of the earth—sprung of the splendor of the Vasus, born of the might of the Vasus—has gone to the Vasus themselves, mourn now your wealth, your sons, the earth, the Kurus, and this whole host.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca mahāprabhāve varade nipātite; lokaśreṣṭhe śāṃtanave mahaujasi parājiteṣu bharateṣu durmanāḥ; karṇo bhṛśaṃ nyaśvasad aśru vartayan
english: Saṃjaya said: When the boon-granting son of Śaṃtanu, of great splendor and mighty energy, the foremost in the world, was struck down, and the Bhāratas were vanquished, Karṇa, downcast, sighed long and let his tears fall.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu rādheyavaco niśamya te; sutāś ca rājaṃs tava sainikāś ca ha parasparaṃ cukruśur ārtijaṃ bhṛśaṃ; tadāśru netrair mumucur hi śabdavat
english: And hearing these words of the son of Rādhā, your sons too, O king, and your soldiers, cried out aloud to one another in their anguish, and let fall their tears with sound from their eyes.

sanskrit: pravartamāne tu punar mahāhave; vigāhyamānāsu camūṣu pārthivaiḥ athābravīd dharṣakaraṃ vacas tadā; ratharṣabhān sarvamahāratharṣabhaḥ
english: But as the great battle was joined once more, and the kings plunged into the warring hosts, that bull among all great chariot-warriors then spoke heartening words to those bulls among chariot-warriors:

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca jagaty anitye satataṃ pradhāvati; pracintayann asthiram adya lakṣaye bhavatsu tiṣṭhatsv iha pātito raṇe; giriprakāśaḥ kurupuṃgavaḥ katham
english: Karṇa said: In a world impermanent, forever hastening on, I see plainly today how unstable it is. While you yourselves stood here, how was the bull of the Kurus, like a very mountain, cast down in battle?

sanskrit: nipātite śāṃtanave mahārathe; divākare bhūtalam āsthite yathā na pārthivāḥ soḍhum alaṃ dhanaṃjayaṃ; giripravoḍhāram ivānilaṃ drumāḥ
english: With the great chariot-warrior, the son of Śaṃtanu, struck down—as though the sun had sunk to the earth—the kings can no more withstand Dhanaṃjaya than trees can withstand the wind that carries mountains away.

sanskrit: hatapradhānaṃ tv idam ārtarūpaṃ; parair hatotsāham anātham adya vai mayā kurūṇāṃ paripālyam āhave; balaṃ yathā tena mahātmanā tathā
english: This army of the Kurus, its chief now slain, stricken in look, its spirit broken by the foe, left masterless this day—must be guarded by me in battle as that great soul once guarded it.

sanskrit: samāhitaṃ cātmani bhāram īdṛśaṃ; jagat tathānityam idaṃ ca lakṣaye nipātitaṃ cāhavaśauṇḍam āhave; kathaṃ nu kuryām aham āhave bhayam
english: Such a burden is laid upon me; and I see how impermanent this world is—he, drunk with battle, struck down in battle. How then should I let battle make me afraid?

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu tān kuruvṛṣabhān ajihmagaiḥ; praverayan yamasadanaṃ raṇe caran yaśaḥ paraṃ jagati vibhāvya vartitā; parair hato yudhi śayitātha vā punaḥ
english: As for me, ranging the field and speeding those bulls of the Kurus to the house of Yama with my straight-flying shafts, I shall win the highest glory in the world—or else, struck down by the foe, lie slain in battle.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro dhṛtimatidharmatattvavān; vṛkodaro gajaśatatulyavikramaḥ tathārjunas tridaśavarātmajo yato; na tad balaṃ sujayam athāmarair api
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, firm and versed in the very truth of dharma; Vṛkodara, whose valor equals a hundred elephants; and Arjuna, son of the foremost of the gods—because of them, that host is not easily conquered even by the immortals.

sanskrit: yamau raṇe yatra yamopamau bale; sasātyakir yatra ca devakīsutaḥ na tad balaṃ kāpuruṣo 'bhyupeyivān; nivartate mṛtyumukhād ivāsakṛt
english: Where in battle stand the twins, the equals of Yama in strength, and where stands the son of Devakī with Sātyaki—no coward who comes against that host but turns back, again and again, as if from the very jaws of death.

sanskrit: tapo 'bhyudīrṇaṃ tapasaiva gamyate; balaṃ balenāpi tathā manasvibhiḥ manaś ca me śatrunivāraṇe dhruvaṃ; svarakṣaṇe cācalavad vyavasthitam
english: Towering austerity is met only by austerity, and strength too by strength, so the wise hold; and my mind is fixed, unshaken as a mountain, upon repelling the foe and upon guarding my own.

sanskrit: evaṃ caiṣāṃ budhyamānaḥ prabhāvaṃ; gatvaivāhaṃ tāñ jayāmy adya sūta mitradroho marṣaṇīyo na me 'yaṃ; bhagne sainye yaḥ sahāyaḥ sa mitram
english: And though I well know their might, I shall go forth this very day, O charioteer, and conquer them. Betrayal of a friend is not to be borne by me: he who stands by you when the army is broken—he is the true friend.

sanskrit: kartāsmy etat satpuruṣāryakarma; tyaktvā prāṇān anuyāsyāmi bhīṣmam sarvān saṃkhye śatrusaṃghān haniṣye; hatas tair vā vīralokaṃ gamiṣye
english: This noble deed worthy of a true man I shall do: laying down my life, I shall follow after Bhīṣma. I shall slay all the throngs of the foe in battle, or, slain by them, shall go to the world of heroes.

sanskrit: saṃprākruṣṭe ruditastrīkumāre; parābhūte pauruṣe dhārtarāṣṭre mayā kṛtyam iti jānāmi sūta; tasmāc chatrūn dhārtarāṣṭrasya jeṣye
english: When the women and children wail and weep aloud, and the manhood of the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra is brought low, then there is something I must do—this I know, O charioteer; and so I shall vanquish the foes of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son.

sanskrit: kurūn rakṣan pāṇḍuputrāñ jighāṃsaṃs; tyaktvā prāṇān ghorarūpe raṇe 'smin sarvān saṃkhye śatrusaṃghān nihatya; dāsyāmy ahaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāya rājyam
english: Guarding the Kurus, seeking to slay the sons of Pāṇḍu, casting away my life in this battle of dread aspect, having struck down all the throngs of the foe in the field, I shall give the kingdom to the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: nibadhyatāṃ me kavacaṃ vicitraṃ; haimaṃ śubhraṃ maṇiratnāvabhāsi śirastrāṇaṃ cārkasamānabhāsaṃ; dhanuḥ śarāṃś cāpi viṣāhikalpān
english: Let my wondrous armor be bound on—golden, gleaming bright with gems and jewels—and my helmet too, radiant as the sun, my bow, and my arrows like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: upāsaṅgān ṣoḍaśa yojayantu; dhanūṃṣi divyāni tathāharantu asīṃś ca śaktīś ca gadāś ca gurvīḥ; śaṅkhaṃ ca jāmbūnadacitrabhāsam
english: Let them fit on sixteen quivers, and bring forth divine bows as well, and swords and spears and heavy maces, and a conch bright with the sheen of Jāmbūnada gold.

sanskrit: etāṃ raukmīṃ nāgakakṣyāṃ ca jaitrīṃ; jaitraṃ ca me dhvajam indīvarābham ślakṣṇair vastrair vipramṛjyānayasva; citrāṃ mālāṃ cātra baddhvā sajālām
english: This golden elephant-girth that brings victory, and my victorious banner with the hue of the blue lotus—wipe them clean with soft cloths and bring them to me, and bind upon it a bright garland with its netting.

sanskrit: aśvān agryān pāṇḍurābhraprakāśān; puṣṭān snātān mantrapūtābhir adbhiḥ taptair bhāṇḍaiḥ kāñcanair abhyupetāñ; śīghrāñ śīghraṃ sūtaputrānayasva
english: My finest horses, gleaming like pale clouds, well-fed, bathed, and washed with waters hallowed by sacred chants, decked with vessels of refined gold and swift of foot—bring them quickly, O charioteer's son.

sanskrit: rathaṃ cāgryaṃ hemajālāvanaddhaṃ; ratnaiś citraṃ candrasūryaprakāśaiḥ dravyair yuktaṃ saṃprahāropapannair; vāhair yuktaṃ tūrṇam āvartayasva
english: And my excellent chariot, bound about with a net of gold, bright with jewels that shine like moon and sun, furnished with the gear that battle requires and yoked with its steeds—wheel it swiftly round to me.

sanskrit: citrāṇi cāpāni ca vegavanti; jyāś cottamāḥ saṃhananopapannāḥ tūṇāṃś ca pūrṇān mahataḥ śarāṇām; āsajya gātrāvaraṇāni caiva
english: And the splendid swift bows, and the finest bowstrings of firm make, and the great quivers full of arrows—lay these all together, and the guards for the limbs as well.

sanskrit: prāyātrikaṃ cānayatāśu sarvaṃ; kanyāḥ pūrṇaṃ vīrakāṃsyaṃ ca haimam ānīya mālām avabadhya cāṅge; pravādayantv āśu jayāya bherīḥ
english: And let them quickly bring all that befits the march, the maidens, and the golden hero's-cup brimming full; and having brought a garland and bound it upon my body, let them straightway sound the drums for victory.

sanskrit: prayāhi sūtāśu yataḥ kirīṭī; vṛkodaro dharmasuto yamau ca tān vā haniṣyāmi sametya saṃkhye; bhīṣmāya vaiṣyāmi hato dviṣadbhiḥ
english: Drive on swiftly, O charioteer, to where the Diademed one is, and Vṛkodara, the son of Dharma, and the twins. Either I shall slay them, joining battle in the field, or, struck down by the foe, I shall go the way of Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: yasmin rājā satyadhṛtir yudhiṣṭhiraḥ; samāsthito bhīmasenārjunau ca vāsudevaḥ sātyakiḥ sṛñjayāś ca; manye balaṃ tad ajayyaṃ mahīpaiḥ
english: That host in which stand King Yudhiṣṭhira, steadfast in truth, and Bhīmasena and Arjuna, and Vāsudeva, Sātyaki, and the Sṛñjayas—that host, I deem, is unconquerable by the kings of earth.
